title: CLR/103/2016 of Vikram Chand Karnwal AND OTHERS Vs Anil Kumar AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CLR No. 103 of 2016
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for
the revisionists.
Mr. H.M. Bhatia, Advocate for the
caveators/respondent nos.2 and 3.
Having heard learned counsel for
the revisionists as well as learned counsel
for the caveators, it transpires that SCC
Suit No.11 of 2010 was instituted for rent
and eviction of the disputed shop. Such
shop was given in tenancy to the
predecessors in interest of defendant
nos.1 to 7.
On 18.07.2011, service upon the
defendant nos.4 to 7 was deemed
sufficient and the Suit was directed to
proceed ex-parte against them.
A compromise was entered into
between the plaintiff (landlord) and
defendant nos.1 to 3 to the effect that
rent of such shop will be enhanced to the
tune of Rs.3,000/- w.e.f. 19.09.2012 and
thereafter, Rs.1,000/- will be added after
every four years.
After lapse of quarter over a year,
plaintiff again filed SCC Suit No.01 of
2014, which is pending adjudication
before the Court below.
Defendant contested such Suit
and during the course of trial, he moved
an amendment application on 15
January, 2015 depicting the fact of
compromise in the previous Suit, as
indicated above.
After closure of evidence of both
the parties, the Suit is pending for
hearing of arguments since 12.04.2016.
Learned Court below accepted six
to seven adjournments at the instance of
defendants but instead of putting forth

the submissions, defendant moved
another amendment application under
Order 6 Rule 17 CPC entailing almost
similar facts, as have been highlighted in
the compromise dated 19.07.2012 in the
previous suit.
So, learned Court below has
rejected the amendment application
referring the proviso of Order 6 Rule 17
CPC.
I do not find any infirmity in the
impugned order, therefore, this revision is
dismissed at the threshold.
